page.layout: Running head at top, with page number 185 at top right. One column of running text. Below the last line: signature "M 5" at the left foot and catchword "rosa-" at the right foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: stione.Quòd si ipsum nutricis lac aquosius sit, tūc nihil, aut parum mutata victus ratio-ne, sanguine expurgabimus hydragogijs pharmacijs, ad bonãq; tum temperiem, tū consistentiam reducemus. Si prꝫterea aliis excrementis vitiatus sit sanguis, similiter purgabitur pro cacochymiæ differentia. Si vero copia linquat, tum phlebotomia[?] leuabitur. Ipsis non subscribimus, qui infanti e-pileptico nihil esse moliendum existimāt: imò vero ipsi (quantum fieri poterit) auxiliari convenit. Idcirco primùm ab iis omnibus, quæ repentinum metum & terrorem incutiunt, cuiusmodi sunt tympanorum soni, tonitrua, fulgura, voces clangosę, furio-sorum vociferationes, & alia id genus terrifica avocetur. Deinde curabit nutrix'ne immoderatis vigilijs, aut clamoribus, aut ferventi calore ignis solisve, aut frigore, afficiatur suus alumnus. Videbit quoq; ne nimio somno idem opprimatur. Leviter etiam purgabitur infans, si quantulamcun-que ferat evacuationem. Propterea vomitoria ex hydromelite liquido, illi parabimus: aut ex eodem clysteres. Item saccharum rosatum, laxatiuum, aut eius loco syrupum rosatum, itidem laxatiuum, aut mel rosa-

page.notes: The glyph after "phlebotomia" is unclear (possibly a printed mark or damaged letter); "leuabitur" is read from the visible "eua bitur". "prꝫterea" has a doubtful abbreviation mark. "clangosę" ends in a doubtful ę. The running head was printed in small capitals with V for the vowel of CAUSAS; it is given with U per the spelling rule. The final line is the catchword, not included in the paragraph text beyond "rosa-", which is repeated there as printed.
